quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Improper braking:

options.text: Should not be a concern, since the motorcycle has two brakes.

questions.explanation: Improper braking causes many motorcycle crashes. Using correct braking technique is an important part of safe riding.

questions.question: When riding, you should wear:
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing to make yourself more visible to other drivers. Clothing with reflective materials also helps.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, it is important to:

options.text: Focus only on what is in front of you.
Focus only on what is behind you.
Know what is happening both in front and behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know what is happening both in front and behind you.
questions.explanation: You must be aware of traffic ahead of you. But you also need to watch what is behind you. Check your mirrors regularly to see what is coming from behind.

questions.question: Blind spots on motorcycles:

options.text: Should be regularly checked by riders.
Don't exist if the motorcycle has a rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be regularly checked by riders.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Make this a regular habit.

questions.question: Use your mirrors when stopping at an intersection:

options.text: To see if drivers behind you notice you are stopping.
To look for dark clouds that may indicate poor weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: To see if drivers behind you notice you are stopping.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors at intersections to make sure drivers approaching from behind see you and your actions. This helps you know if they are paying attention to you.

questions.question: The best clothing for a motorcyclist:

options.text: Should not stand out to other drivers.

questions.explanation: Good riding clothing protects you in a crash. It should also keep you comfortable and make you visible to other drivers.

questions.question: You should pick a lane position that:

options.text: Makes you visible and keeps safe space around you.
You like, without thinking about others.
Gets you close to other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes you visible and keeps safe space around you.
questions.explanation: Position yourself where other drivers can see you and where you have space around your motorcycle. No single lane position is always best. Change your position as road conditions change.

questions.question: A good way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Let them pass by slowing down or changing lanes.
Speed up to put distance between you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let them pass by slowing down or changing lanes.
questions.explanation: If you can do so safely, change lanes and let the tailgater pass. Speeding up may make them tailgate you at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You may proceed through the intersection with caution.
You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red traffic light. You must come to a complete stop and wait until you get a signal that allows you to turn in your direction.

questions.question: When being followed by a tailgater, you should:

options.text: Not change how you are riding.

questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. Speeding up may make them tailgate you at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: What should you do when nearing a blind intersection?

options.text: Assume other drivers will yield the right-of-way.
Move to a lane position that makes you more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a lane position that makes you more visible.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, move to the lane position that other drivers can see you best.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that traffic is merging.

questions.question: What is the best way to help others see your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times. Most motorcycles made after 1978 turn on the headlight automatically when running. Check that your headlight works before every ride.

questions.question: When scanning around your motorcycle, what should you look for?

options.text: Potential escape routes near intersections, shopping areas, or schools.
Whether you can travel faster than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Potential escape routes near intersections, shopping areas, or schools.
questions.explanation: Look for escape routes at intersections, shopping areas, schools, and construction zones.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should riders do?

options.text: Follow each other as closely as possible.
Not worry about distances between members.

questions.explanation: Ride in a staggered formation. This allows riders to stay together while maintaining safe following distances.

questions.question: When entering a turn, when should you change gears?

options.text: Take the motorcycle out of gear.

questions.explanation: Change gears before entering a turn. If you must change gears during the turn, do it smoothly.

questions.question: What does the "S" stand for in "SIPDE"?
questions.explanation: SIPDE is a five-step process for safe riding. The letters stand for Scan, Identify, Predict, Decide, and Execute.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe.
Only stop to yield to other traffic.
Vehicles will be entering the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Stop completely, yield to all crossing traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.

questions.question: When choosing a riding jacket, it should:

options.text: Fit loosely and flap in the wind.
Fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind.
Not be made of leather or sturdy material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind.
questions.explanation: Choose a leather or sturdy jacket that fits snugly without flapping in the wind. It should also be loose enough to let you move freely.

questions.question: How should a protective jacket fit?

options.text: Loose and flapping in the wind.

questions.explanation: Jackets should fit snugly so they do not flap, but not so tight that they limit your movement.

questions.question: Should you wear gloves while riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Yes. Your hands may get cold while riding.
Yes. They improve your grip and protect your hands.
No. Gloves can get in the way of the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes. They improve your grip and protect your hands.
questions.explanation: Wearing gloves while riding improves your grip and protects your hands. Choose full-fingered gloves made of durable material.

questions.question: For the most protection, your helmet should:
questions.explanation: Your helmet gives the best protection when it meets DOT and state standards, fits snugly all the way around, and has no damage.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid fatigue on a long motorcycle ride?
questions.explanation: On a long trip, limit your riding time each day and take frequent rest breaks to avoid fatigue. Do not use artificial stimulants because you may feel very tired when they wear off.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They warn drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce the chances of a collision?

options.text: Focus only on your riding, not on other drivers.

questions.explanation: Wearing bright or reflective clothing makes you more visible to other drivers and lowers your risk of a collision. Always watch the drivers around you to prepare for their next moves.
